Technology Executive | AI Engineering | Strategic Growth
I’m a senior technology executive and hands-on engineer with nearly 20 years of experience building enterprise platforms, driving AI innovation, and leading technology transformation across government and industry. As a former DHS Chief Technology Officer and Chief AI Officer, I oversaw a $10 billion federal IT portfolio and delivered AI capabilities at enterprise scale. I combine engineering expertise with strategic growth, business development, and executive leadership to turn emerging technologies into measurable mission and business outcomes.
I believe effective technology leadership requires understanding the entire lifecycle of innovation: identifying the problem, designing the solution, building the technology, earning organizational adoption, and delivering measurable value. My career has let me approach that lifecycle as a software engineer, enterprise architect, federal CTO, AI executive, commercial solution engineer, and senior leader in a growing government technology company.

AI Engineering & Innovation: I build AI systems that solve real problems. From generative AI and intelligent automation to secure enterprise platforms and responsible governance, I help organizations move beyond experimentation and make emerging technology practical, secure, and valuable.

Technology Leadership & Transformation: I’ve led engineering teams and enterprise transformation across government and industry. Successful transformation takes strong teams, a clear strategy, an understanding of organizational culture, and the ability to turn ambitious goals into executable plans.

Strategic Growth & Business Development: I connect technology with business strategy through federal sales, technical capture, customer engagement, and differentiated solutions. My experience includes opportunity shaping, executive management briefings, and M&A technology due diligence.

Hands-On Engineering & Product Development: I’ve never stopped being an engineer. I design architectures, write code, and build applications, exploring distributed systems, cloud-native infrastructure, AI orchestration, automation, and data platforms. Staying hands-on is part of being an effective technology leader.

Strategy Is Important. Execution Is Everything.: A great technology strategy should be ambitious enough to change what’s possible and practical enough to implement. That requires understanding the technology, the organization, and the people who depend on the outcome. Sometimes the greatest improvements come from simplifying processes, reusing proven capabilities, or removing unnecessary complexity.

Build Capabilities, Not Just Projects: A successful project solves an immediate problem. A well-designed platform can help an organization solve an entire class of problems. I look for opportunities to create reusable AI infrastructure, development platforms, automation, and shared services, while being deliberate about where standardization creates value beyond the original use case.

Make Innovation Accessible: Transformation succeeds when people across an organization can participate. AI literacy, workforce development, and practical education help the people closest to a problem apply technology to their work. My role is to create the environment, tools, and guardrails that empower them to innovate responsibly.

Connect Technology to Outcomes: Complexity is never the objective. What matters is whether a solution improves customer experience, reduces operational friction, accelerates delivery, or creates new opportunities. Effective technology leaders move between vision, architecture, engineering, organizational change, and measurable results.

Technology has always been both my profession and my hobby. I’m a lifelong gamer, from classic RPGs and strategy games to first-person shooters and MMOs. I enjoy exploring game engines and how interactive experiences bring together technology, design, and storytelling. I also enjoy Dungeons & Dragons, 3D printing, home automation, electronics, and experimenting with development tools. Whether I’m building an AI application or a home project, I’m usually learning something new.

Dave Larrimore is a technology executive, AI engineer, and former federal Chief Technology Officer with nearly 20 years of experience driving enterprise modernization, technology innovation, and business growth. He has served in senior leadership roles at DHS and ICE, overseeing large-scale technology portfolios and advancing enterprise cloud and AI capabilities. As Senior Vice President of Solution Engineering at Amivero, he combined hands-on AI engineering with technology strategy and business development. His work included enterprise AI platforms and proprietary automation that increased the business development pipeline by 150% and reduced proposal development time by 60%. He also supported executive management briefings and technology due diligence during Amivero’s acquisition by Xpect Solutions in 2026. Dave remains an active technologist, building software and exploring AI, product engineering, and organizational transformation.
